annotations.text:
(Recommended) Hero D · axis: framed portrait.
Why: it is Hero B's copy column (H1, lead, both CTAs, four credentials, availability pill, all lifted) with the four-tile mosaic replaced by the live homepage hero photo in the for-sale .chero frame (22px radius, 1280/960, same shadow), so it is the one hero of the three whose every element already ships somewhere on the site. Measured at 1440 the #hero-grid is 385.8px (range 350 to 400), and its Mobile root is 862px, the shortest of the round with F at 863px and E at 1071px. One image above the fold means the LCP asset is the same single hero-midland.webp the live page already loads; E adds two more requests before the H1 at 390.
Trade-off: the inventory is asserted by the pill, not shown. Evie ($1,500) and Roys ($2,300) leave the hero, and the Desktop ribbon wraps its fourth credential onto a second line because the copy column is the narrower 1.08fr of the .chero split.

Hero E · axis: lead photo + pair.
Why: it is the only one of the three that keeps Hero B's named-bird evidence (Evie, Timneh $1,500; Roys, Congo $2,300, prices per data/price-matrix.json) while still leading with the live hero-midland.webp, so the claim on the pill is backed by two priced birds in the same viewport. Desktop #hero-grid measures 389.5px, inside the 350 to 400 range, with the right column set at 370px so the wide tile (156px) plus two square tiles with captions beneath (233px) fit the band.
Trade-off: it is the tallest Mobile hero at 1071px (209px more than D) because three photos stack above the H1 at 390, and the wide tile is only 156px tall at Desktop, which crops the Midland, Texas sign to a strip.

Hero F · axis: credential band.
Why: it moves the four credentials out of the copy column into a full-width band on #234f3b along the hero's bottom edge, which shortens the copy column to 260px at Desktop and lets the photo run as a 300 x 322 portrait; the #hero-grid measures exactly 380px at 1440 (322 photo + 16 gap + 42 band), the tightest fit of the three. The band gives the credentials one row at Desktop and a 2 x 2 grid at Tablet and Mobile with the same SVG check, and the availability pill sits on the photo so nothing hangs outside the frame. Mobile root is 863px.
Trade-off: at 390 the band lands below both CTAs at about 590px from the top of the hero, so the credentials are the last thing read rather than the line under the H1 that Hero B and the for-sale ribbon put them on, and the 300px-wide photo is the narrowest hero image of the round.

Counter D · axis: icon stat cards. Four white 16px-radius cards on cream, warm shadow, 20px forest stroke icon + Newsreader numeral in clay #b04228 + 12px uppercase forest label; 4-up at 1440, 2x2 at 768 and 390.
Why: the biggest visual departure from the live strip, and the only one where each stat reads as its own object, so the four claims scan as four proofs rather than one line of numbers.
Trade-off: tallest of the three. Measured section (root minus the 100px hero stub): 192px at 1440, 334px at 768, 294px at 390. Under the ~649px live hero plus the 96px header it lands at ~937px at 1440, past a 900px fold, and at 390 it pushes the bird cards ~157px further down than E.

(Recommended) Counter E · axis: green-tint band. Numeral and label side by side in one row per stat on rgba(45,106,79,.08) over cream, forest #2D6A4F numerals, 1px vertical hairlines between stats at 1440 and 768, 2x2 at 390.
Why: shortest measured section of the three: 86px at 1440, 82px at 768, 137px at 390 (roots 186/182/237 incl. the 100px stub). It is the only variation that keeps the whole counter inside a 900px desktop fold under the ~649px hero + 96px header (745 + 86 = 831px) without touching the hero, and the tint plus the 1px rule gives the hero/counter seam two separations, not one. Contrast measured: forest numerals and #5b524a labels both clear 4.5:1 on the blended tint; probe 0 overflow, 0 contrast fails.
Trade-off: the least dramatic change from the live strip, and the two-word labels wrap to two lines at 768 and 390 (CITES Documented, Floor Price, Reply Guarantee), which reads fine but is not the single-line label the live strip has.

Counter F · axis: seam card. All four stats in ONE white pill card (radius 50px at 1440, 28px at 768, 24px at 390) with margin-top:-40px so it straddles the hero/counter seam; warm shadow; the section's 1px rule and cream tone shift stay visible on both sides of the card.
Why: pulls the credentials up into the hero's viewport: only 56px of new height lands below the seam at 1440 (216 root, 120 stub, 40px overlap) and 96px at 768, so it is nearly as fold-friendly as E while looking the most premium.
Trade-off: the 40px overlap eats the bottom of the hero, and the round-2 hero brief puts the 2x2 credential ribbon and the CTAs at the hero's bottom edge at 390, so the card will collide with them unless the hero adds 40px of bottom padding, which gives that height back. At 390 the section is 170px, 33px more than E.

Dial D · axis: progress line (no ring).
Why: the 64px ring reports one number (1 of 18) and nothing about structure; the 2px track with eighteen numbered nodes shows position and the four part groups at once, and the active node in clay #c8472f with a white numeral is the strongest position marker of the three. Measured at 1440: card 196 × 635px, rows 26px minimum at .74rem, tag pill on every row, numerals #6b625a on cream nodes.
Trade-off: 41px taller than A (594px) because the three part labels each take a line and two of them wrap in the 148px label column, and a track implies a reading order the homepage does not have; buyers land on Available or Pricing and skip the rest.

(Recommended) Dial E · axis: two columns.
Why: measured at 1440 the card is 392 × 337px, 57% of A (594px), and it is the only one of the three that fits under the 772px sticky cap on a 768px-tall laptop (640px usable under a 96px header plus 16px offset), where A at 594px and D at 635px scroll inside the card. Nothing was shrunk to get there: rows stay 27px at .74rem, the tag pill shows on all eighteen, part boundaries are 1px hairlines above 04, 07 and 11, and a 2px progress bar replaces the ring. The body column keeps 680px on the 1140 frame, still wider than the 66ch paragraph max-width, so no reading width is lost.
Trade-off: the card is twice the shipped .tdial width (392 against 196), so the grid template on the live pages changes, and eighteen clay tag pills now sit in a denser block than in A.

Dial F · axis: collapsed parts.
Why: the homepage's four parts already name the reading structure; collapsing the three inactive parts to a header with a real count chip (3, 4 and 8 sections) keeps the ring and cuts the card to 196 × 440px at 1440, 154px shorter than A (594px), while the counts still add to 18 without opening anything.
Trade-off: 15 of the 18 sections are behind a click, and the open/closed state needs a script the shipped .tdial does not carry, so it is the only one of the three that is not a pure CSS swap.

(Recommended) Rail D · axis: part select.
Why: the 18 sections already sit in four named parts, and the live bottom sheet earned its place by being the only pattern that shows part names on a 390 screen (round-1 rail-c-note). D keeps that advantage at the TOP of the page under the 96px header, where hardening 1b says the rail belongs, and at zero taps: with Part Four open the pill set drops from 18 to 8, so the active pill (13 Shipping) sits centred with a neighbour visible either side at 390, where round-1 Rail A showed about three of eighteen. Rail is 60px tall; every control 44px; pills are the round-1 Rail A pill unchanged.
Trade-off: moving to another part costs two taps (open the part list, pick a part) and the button must be wired with scroll-spy so the part label and pill set follow the reader; drawn only in its closed state here.

Rail E · axis: progress.
Why: the thinnest rail of the three at 48px (round-1 Rail A is 62px, D and F are 60px), and the only one whose state is legible without scrolling the rail itself: Section 13 of 18 plus a 2px clay line filled to 72.2% tells the reader where they are in an 18-section page at a glance. Both chevron buttons are 44 by 44 and the row never overflows at 390.
Trade-off: it navigates one section at a time, so reaching a far section costs up to 17 taps and the part names disappear entirely; it is a position readout more than a jump-link rail.

Rail F · axis: icon chips.
Why: a single forest-filled marker on a row of quiet white hairline chips reads as one strip instead of eighteen clay outlines, and a 16px icon gives each section a second cue at scan speed. Chips are 44px tall, 8px gaps, 60px rail.
Trade-off: the icon plus label makes each chip 100 to 140px wide, so 390 shows about three chips of eighteen (the same reach problem as Rail A) and the eighteen icons are new artwork to draw and maintain; eight of the section names have no obvious icon, which is why the drawn set leans on generic glyphs.

Table Cvt D · axis: column cards.
Why: Mobile is one card per species (Congo, then Timneh) listing all 12 traits as label: value pairs, so a buyer reads one bird top to bottom the way the live for-sale pages present a single bird. Tablet puts the two cards side by side; Desktop is a classic 4-column table with the Timneh column tinted rgba(45,106,79,.08) because the three decided Edge rows in the round-1 copy (Price, Maturity, Temperament) all go to Timneh, and a 16px check marks each of those rows. Measured Mobile root 1582px (round-1 A was 3,398px, B 1,661px), Tablet 935px, Desktop 980px. Probe: 0 overflow, 0 hit targets under 44, 0 contrast fails, min Mobile text 14px.
Trade-off: on Mobile the Congo value for a trait is a full card-scroll away from the Timneh value, so row-by-row comparison is the weakest of the three; the Edge chips live only in the Timneh card.

Table Cvt E · axis: banded rows.
Why: each trait is a full-width warm band (#f6efe8, uppercase) carrying the Edge verdict at its right end, with the Congo and Timneh values in a 2-up grid under it at every width, so the two values sit next to each other on a phone without any toggle, tab or script. Desktop keeps the identical bands inside a 1px-bordered 18px-radius container at max-width 960 centered, so the same DOM serves all three viewports. Measured Mobile root 1556px, Tablet 1405px, Desktop 1450px. Probe: 0 overflow, 0 contrast fails, min Mobile text 14px.
Trade-off: it is the tallest of the three at Desktop (1450px versus 980px for D and 873px for F) because every trait spends a band plus a value row, and the Desktop 960 container leaves the 1120 content width partly unused.

(Recommended) Table Cvt F · axis: accordion rows.
Why: Mobile is twelve native <details> rows, each summary 48px tall showing the trait name and the leading species (a green check plus Timneh on the three decided rows, Compare on the nine even ones), expanding to both values and the Edge line; the first row ships open. It is the shortest Mobile answer measured this round at 1056px, against 1582px for D, 1556px for E and 3,398px for round-1 A, so the whole comparison fits in roughly two phone screens and the verdict for every trait is visible before a single tap. Desktop and Tablet are a hairline table with no vertical rules, 1px row rules and a 16px inline SVG check in the leading cell, 873px at 1440, the lightest of the three. Zero JavaScript: <details> is native. Probe: 0 overflow, 0 hit targets under 44, 0 contrast fails.
Trade-off: the values themselves are hidden until a tap on Mobile, so a buyer who wants the numbers rather than the verdict taps up to twelve times; the collapsed default also keeps that text out of the first paint for crawlers that do not expand details.

Table Mvf D · axis: column cards.
Why: same construction as Cvt D so the two tables read as one system: Mobile one card per sex (Male, Female) with the three buyer questions as label: value pairs plus a separate Telling them apart card carrying the DNA-sexing fact verbatim; Tablet 2-up; Desktop a 3-column classic table with the fact as a colspan row. No column is tinted: the round-1 copy names no winner in any of the three rows, so there is no C.A.Gs pick to shade, and shading one would invent a verdict. Measured Mobile root 907px, Tablet 594px, Desktop 500px. Probe clean.
Trade-off: with only three traits the two Mobile cards are mostly header and padding, and the male value for a question sits a card-scroll away from the female value.

(Recommended) Table Mvf E · axis: banded rows.
Why: the three buyer questions are long-sentence answers (the longest cell is 71 characters), which is exactly the content that broke the live table at 375 in round 1 (one or two words per line). A full-width question band with the Male and Female answers in a 2-up grid under it gives each answer half the width at every viewport with the two answers adjacent, and the Telling them apart fact becomes a fourth band with a full-width paragraph, so nothing is hidden and nothing scrolls sideways. Measured Mobile root 765px, Tablet 598px, Desktop 598px in the 960 container. Probe: 0 overflow, 0 contrast fails, min Mobile text 14px.
Trade-off: it is taller than F on Mobile (765px versus 459px) because every answer is shown at once, and half-width columns at 390 wrap the longer answers to three lines.

Table Mvf F · axis: accordion rows.
Why: Mobile is four native <details> rows (three questions plus the fact), 48px summaries, the first open; because no row has a winner every summary reads Compare, and the fact row reads Fact. It is the shortest Mvf Mobile board at 459px (D 907px, E 765px). Desktop and Tablet are the hairline table with no vertical rules and 1px row rules; there is no leading cell and therefore no check mark anywhere, which the note says so nobody reads its absence as a missing asset. Probe clean.
Trade-off: with no verdicts to preview, the collapsed summaries carry almost no information (a name and the word Compare), so the buyer must open all four rows to learn anything; the accordion pays its cost without earning it here.

Axis D: column cards.
Why: Mobile is one card per species (390 wide, 1266 px tall measured), so all 12 values are readable without a tap; Tablet 2-up (715 px); Desktop is the classic 4-column table at 426 px with the African Grey row tinted rgba(45,106,79,.08) and a C.A.Gs pick chip.
Trade-off: the tallest mobile answer of the three (1266 px vs 845 for E and 635 for F); a buyer scrolls three screens to reach Amazon.

Axis E: banded rows.
Why: each trait is a full-width warm band with a 2x2 grid of species under it, so the comparison is trait-first (what buyers scan for); the African Grey cell is tinted green with a check in every band. Same structure at all widths: Mobile 845 px, Tablet 821 px, Desktop 850 px inside a 960px bordered container.
Trade-off: species names repeat three times; the tallest Desktop of the three (850 px vs 426 D, 425 F).

(Recommended) Axis F: accordion rows.
Why: Mobile is three <details> rows (summaries 44px+) whose summary carries the African Grey value inline, so the pick is visible with zero taps at 635 px tall, about half of D (1266) and under E (845); Desktop is a hairline table at 425 px with no vertical rules and a 16px SVG check in the African Grey cell, the lightest of the three.
Trade-off: 8 of the 12 values (Macaw, Cockatoo, Amazon) sit behind a tap on Mobile; only the first row opens by default.

Axis D: column cards.
Why: Mobile is one card per subspecies (390 wide, 1649 px measured) with the price as a 28px Newsreader numeral at the top and the three traits as label:value lines, so every price is readable without a tap; Tablet 2-up (886 px); Desktop is the classic clay-header table at 572 px, zebra warm-bed rows, with the Congo Grey Baby row tinted rgba(45,106,79,.08) and a Top pick chip. Closest to the live PricingTable, so the smallest change for the breeder.
Trade-off: the second-tallest Mobile of the three (1649 px vs 2064 E and 834 F); a buyer scrolls four screens to reach Fertile Egg.

Axis E: banded rows.
Why: each subspecies is a warm-bed band carrying the label left and the price right, with Adult weight, Best fit and Talking ability in a 3-up grid under it (1-up at Mobile), so the price sits on the band the eye lands on first; the Top pick cells are green-tinted. Desktop 1067 px inside a 960px 18px-radius container, Tablet 1016 px, Mobile 2064 px.
Trade-off: the tallest at every width (2064 px Mobile, 1067 Desktop vs 572 D and 570 F); six bands of three cells means 18 trait cells, so the six-row pricing table becomes a long read.

(Recommended) Axis F: accordion rows.
Why: Mobile is six <details> rows (summaries 44px+) whose summary carries subspecies and price, so all six prices read with zero taps at 834 px, half of D (1649) and 40% of E (2064); Desktop is a hairline table at 570 px with no vertical rules and a 16px SVG check on the Congo Grey Baby row, the lightest footprint of the three; Tablet keeps the same table at 606 px.
Trade-off: weight, fit and talking ability are behind a tap on Mobile for five of six rows; only the first row opens by default.

(Recommended) Faq D · axis: search-first.
Why: the breeder's screenshot is filed as "faq section-too long" and the live section measures 2404px at Mobile. D keeps all twenty-one questions on the page as 48px one-line summaries with only the first open, and measures 1830px at Mobile (24% under live), 1750px at Tablet and 1299px at Desktop, where two columns of eleven and ten put every question above one screen. It is the shortest of the three round-2 mobiles, and the search field plus topic chips answer the twenty-one-item scale directly: a buyer types "deposit" instead of scanning.
Trade-off: the search field is drawn, so the live build needs a few lines of script to filter the summaries; without it the chips and field are decoration. Round-one C still wins on raw height (1434px) because it hides seventeen questions behind one control, which D refuses to do.

Faq E · axis: quick answers + rest.
Why: the six highest-intent questions (CITES, cost, shipping, DNA sexing, deposit, lifespan) are answered in cards with the first sentence of the live answer, so a buyer reads the fact with zero taps. The other fifteen sit under a "15 more questions" eyebrow as a plain accordion, all closed. Measured 1597px at Desktop (3-up), 1718px at Tablet (2-up) and 2144px at Mobile (1-up).
Trade-off: it is the tallest of the three at Mobile, only 11% under the live 2404px, because six stacked cards cost more than six closed rows. The card copy is the answer's first sentence, so "Yes." answers carry their second sentence too; the full answer is not on the card.

Faq F · axis: side-nav.
Why: the three round-one topics (5 / 7 / 9 questions) become a sticky 240px topic list with counts beside a grouped accordion, so the reader sees the map and the questions at once instead of tabbing. Measured 1743px at Desktop, 1780px at Tablet and 1898px at Mobile, where the list turns into a scrolling pills row over the same accordion.
Trade-off: the sticky card assumes the 96px header offset and spends 272px of desktop width on navigation for three items; at Mobile it is D without the search field and 68px taller, so it only earns its place on Desktop and Tablet.

Shipping D · axis: tier chooser.
Why: the two tiers become two equal white cards with the price as a 44px Newsreader numeral and a what-is-included list, so a buyer comparing $185 against $350 reads the difference as five checked lines per card instead of two paragraphs; every line is a fact already in the round-1 tier copy or intro, and one clay CTA sits under both cards. Measured: Desktop 1,087px, Tablet 1,140px, Mobile 1,753px.
Trade-off: it is the tallest of the three at every width, and the tallest on the page at 390 by 357px over F, because the two lists stack; it also drops the crate photo entirely.

(Recommended) Shipping E · axis: route.
Why: the route line puts both prices on the trip itself, Midland, TX to your airport ($185) to your door ($350), in the order the bird travels, and it keeps the crate photo beside the route. Measured it is the shortest of the three at Desktop, 981px against F 1,021 and D 1,087, and at Mobile, 1,380px against F 1,396 and D 1,753, where the line turns vertical with three 20px nodes down the left.
Trade-off: it is the tallest at Tablet, 1,190px against F 1,028 and D 1,140, because the photo stacks above the route there; and at Desktop the three stop descriptions sit in 219px centered columns at 13px, the narrowest measure on the page.

Shipping F · axis: fact grid.
Why: six labelled definitions (tier, price, carrier and route, timing, crate, arrival) answer the six shipping questions without card chrome, beside the crate photo at 22px radius, which is the layout closest to the live section (photo beside copy) and so the cheapest to adopt. Measured it is the shortest at Tablet, 1,028px against D 1,140 and E 1,190, and within 40px of the shortest at Desktop (1,021) and 16px at Mobile (1,396).
Trade-off: the two prices share one 15px value cell instead of leading their tiers, so a reader scanning for a figure finds it third, after Tier, and the grid carries no tier descriptions at all.
